title: Fibrancy of finite iterated pullback towers
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and Kan complexes as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $B$ and $E$ be Kan complexes and let $s,t:E\to B$ be Kan fibrations, meaning maps with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Define $P_1=E$ with endpoint map $t$, and recursively
$$P_k=P_{k-1}\times_{B,t_{k-1},s}E,$$
where $t_{k-1}:P_{k-1}\to B$ is the endpoint map of the last $E$ coordinate. Then every $P_k$ is a Kan complex, for $k\geq2$ the projection $P_k\to P_{k-1}$ is a Kan fibration, and its endpoint map $t_k:P_k\to B$ is a Kan fibration. No nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed on $B$, $E$ or the pullbacks; $k$ ranges over positive integers.

source.place: Kerodon Subsection 3.1.1 (00T0), Remarks 3.1.1.6, 3.1.1.10 and 3.1.1.11: pullback and composition closure of Kan fibrations and fibrancy over a Kan base.

proof.text: We use simultaneous induction on the positive integer $k$: $P_k$ is Kan, $t_k$ is a Kan fibration, and, when $k\geq2$, $\pi_k:P_k\to P_{k-1}$ is a Kan fibration. For $k=1$, $P_1=E$ is Kan and $t_1=t$ is a Kan fibration by hypothesis. For the induction step fix $k\geq2$ and assume the assertions at $k-1$. All pullbacks and their coordinate maps are the degreewise ones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; in particular $t_k=t\circ\operatorname{pr}_E$ and $t_{k-1}\circ\pi_k=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_E$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.1; setup of the finite induction

proof.text: To prove the lifting property for $\pi_k$, fix any horn inclusion $j:H=\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow D=\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$. A lifting problem consists of a map $(a,b):H\to P_k$ and $v:D\to P_{k-1}$ such that $v\circ j=a$ and $t_{k-1}\circ a=s\circ b$. Apply the assumed lifting property of $s$ to $b:H\to E$ over $t_{k-1}\circ v:D\to B$. It gives $\widetilde b:D\to E$ with $\widetilde b\circ j=b$ and $s\circ\widetilde b=t_{k-1}\circ v$. Thus $(v,\widetilde b):D\to P_k$ is a simplicial map by the degreewise pullback definition, restricts to $(a,b)$ and projects to $v$. This solves every lifting problem for $\pi_k$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.1 and Remark 3.1.1.6; explicit pullback lift

proof.text: For the endpoint map $t_k$, take a lifting problem with top map $(a,b):H\to P_k$ and bottom map $c:D\to B$, so $c\circ j=t\circ b$ and $t_{k-1}\circ a=s\circ b$. First lift $b$ through the fibration $t$ over $c$, obtaining $e:D\to E$ with $e\circ j=b$ and $t\circ e=c$. Next apply the induction hypothesis that $t_{k-1}$ is a Kan fibration to the top map $a$ and bottom map $s\circ e$; the needed equality on $H$ is $s\circ e\circ j=s\circ b=t_{k-1}\circ a$. Obtain $w:D\to P_{k-1}$ with $w\circ j=a$ and $t_{k-1}\circ w=s\circ e$. The pair $(w,e):D\to P_k$ extends $(a,b)$ and its endpoint is $t\circ e=c$. Hence $t_k$ is a Kan fibration. These are just two uses of the defining horn lifting properties, with the equality defining the pullback checked explicitly.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.1 and Remarks 3.1.1.6, 3.1.1.10; two successive horn lifts

proof.text: Finally, given a horn map $h:H\to P_k$, first extend $\pi_k\circ h$ to $v:D\to P_{k-1}$ by the Kan property of $P_{k-1}$. Apply the lifting property for $\pi_k$ established in step 2 to $h$ and $v$ to obtain an extension $D\to P_k$. This is exactly the Kan condition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The simultaneous induction is complete. Only horns in positive dimensions were used; if $E$ or a pullback is empty, there are no horn maps into it, so the corresponding lifting and Kan conditions remain valid. If $B$ is empty, the maps $E\to B$ force $E$, and hence all $P_k$, to be empty as well. No surjectivity on vertices or nonemptiness has been used.

source.place: Remark 3.1.1.11; explicit horn filling and completion of induction
